tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
- balanced accuracy (BA)
- Area under the ROC Curve (AUC ROC)

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

We follow the decision guidelines recommended in the study of Maier-Hein et al. [13] for a multi-class,
imbalanced classification problem (certain CoW variants occur more frequent than others).


The most important property for the algorithms is to provide the correct classification of the anterior and
posterior parts of the CoW. Both parts are equally important and will thus be weighted equally. For both parts, the
classification is done in distinct categories and is either fully correct or fully wrong. There is no ‘distance’ between
the classes, where some misclassification receive a lower/higher penalty than others.





 Circle of Willis Intracranial Artery Classification and Quantification Challenge
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Image-level BA scores for anterior- and posterior classification of the CoW on the test set will be computed. For
each score, the best team will receive a rank of 0 and the worst team a rank of 1. All other teams will be ranked
relatively to those performances. The final ranking for this metric will be based on the average of anterior and
posterior classification.


The AUC ROC will be computed per class on the test set. Teams will be ranked relatively to their performances.
The final ranking for this metric will be based on the average ranking position of all classes.


Finally, the ranks for both metrics will be averaged in the overall rank that decides the winning team.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Not applicable. The submitted algorithms will be evaluated on the test set by the challenge organizers.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The ranking scheme allows fair comparison between participating teams and has worked well in previous
challenges organized by our institute (ADAM, WMH).

tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
- Mean absolute error (MAE)
- Pearson correlation coefficient



 Circle of Willis Intracranial Artery Classification and Quantification Challenge

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The MAE is a commonly used and intuitive metric for regression tasks. The Pearson correlation coefficient reflects
the goodness-of-fit for regression models.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

MAE scores for regression on the test set are obtained per angle or diameter. This will yield 25 scores per team. For
each angle or diameter, the best team will receive a rank of 0 and the worst team a rank of 1. All other teams will
be ranked relatively to those performances. The final ranking for this metric will be based on the average of the 25
ranking positions.


The Pearson correlation coefficient will be assessed in a similar manner: per angle or artery the teams will be
ranked relatively to their performances. The final ranking for this metric is the average of the 25 ranking positions.
Finally, the ranks for both metrics will be averaged in the overall rank that decides the winning team.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Not applicable. The submitted algorithms will be evaluated on the test set by the challenge organizers.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The scores for different angles and diameters cannot be directly compared due to differences in scale. Therefore,
we choose to evaluate the results per angle or diameter before obtaining the final average rank. This way, we
ensure equal weighting for both metrics and all classes in the final score.
